newsitem.title: philippines: Manila call loan rates in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates in tight range.

text.p: were stuck in the same band from 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent on Thursday amid a very liquid market, traders said.
The average rate was likewise unchanged at 10.53125 percent. Volume was slightly up at 3.747 billion from 3.683 billion pesos.
"Banks just prefer to place their money overnight with the Central Bank," a big bank dealer said.
Traders said banks did not want to invest their money in term reverse repos because of the new 20 percent tax, which had led to the high liquidity in the market.
The Central Bank is currently borrowing money from the market at an overnight rate of 10.5 percent.
Meanwhile, the secondary market trading of T-bills had banks buying short-term bills and selling the longer-term ones, traders said.
Banks plan to restock their portfolio of longer-term bills when interest rates go up, they said.
"There's pressure for the six months and one year to go up,"a trader said, pointing out cost-push factors that may nudge prices up.
These are the increases in the minimum daily wages in Manila and the impending full deregulation of the oil industry next month which would mean higher oil prices, she said.

A Reuter poll of six institutions showed banks with bid rates of 10.675 to 10.75 for the three-month bills. The six-month bills had offer rates of 11.0 to 11.15 percent; and the one year, 11.40 to 11.50 percent.
